definitions.definition: A person legally recognized as a child's parent. Legal parents can ask for custody and parenting-time orders and have a responsibility to financially support their child.
The legal determination that a person is or is not a child's legal parent. Parentage can be determined by a court order or, when applicable, by a filed Voluntary Declaration of Parentage.
A government form eligible parents can sign and file to create a legal parent-child relationship without first obtaining a parentage judgment in court.
The person who starts a parentage court case.
The other person named in a parentage case who may respond to the petition.
A method of formally notifying another person about the parentage case by having another qualified adult personally deliver the filed court papers.
The final court order in a parentage case that states who the child's legal parents are and may also contain custody, parenting-time, child-support, and other orders.

laws.title: Legal parentage carries rights and responsibilities
laws.statement: Legal parents can ask for custody and visitation (parenting time) orders and are required to financially support their child.

laws.title: Parentage may be required before custody, parenting-time, or support orders
laws.statement: When the people involved are not already both legally recognized as parents, legal parentage generally must be established before the court can make custody, parenting-time, or child-support orders based on their parental status.

laws.title: A filed VDOP has the effect of a parentage judgment
laws.statement: Once a valid Voluntary Declaration of Parentage is filed, it has the same effect as a judgment establishing who the child's legal parents are.

laws.title: VDOP cancellation is time limited
laws.statement: A parent who changes their mind after signing a VDOP generally has only a limited period in which to cancel it; California Courts states that cancellation is easiest within 60 days of signing.

laws.title: Genetics alone does not always determine legal parentage
laws.statement: A judge may consider genetic testing when parentage is disputed, but legal parentage is not determined solely by genetics in every case, and a person can in some circumstances be recognized as a legal parent without a genetic relationship.

laws.title: More than two legal parents may be recognized in limited cases
laws.statement: California Courts states that a child can have more than two legal parents in limited circumstances, including when a judge finds that failing to recognize additional parents would harm the child.

laws.title: Response period after service
laws.statement: After personal service of parentage papers, the other person generally has 30 days to respond. If no response is filed, the case may proceed through a default process.

laws.title: Temporary and final custody orders differ in a parentage case
laws.statement: Custody orders made before entry of the parentage judgment are temporary orders. California Courts explains that changing a final custody order generally requires showing a significant change in circumstances, while changing a temporary order requires showing that the change is in the child's best interests.

procedures.title: Standard parentage case process
procedures.description: California Courts describes a parentage case as a three-stage process to obtain a final determination of legal parentage.
steps: Start a parentage case by completing and filing the required court papers.
Legally notify (serve) the other person.
Finalize the case by agreement or by asking the judge to decide, and submit final forms for the judge to sign.

procedures.title: Start a parentage case
procedures.description: A person asking the court to determine parentage begins by filing the required parentage forms in the appropriate county.
steps: Identify the appropriate family-law court, generally in the county where the child lives or can be found.
Complete Petition to Determine Parental Relationship (FL-200).
Complete Summons (Uniform Parentage — Petition for Custody and Support) (FL-210).
Complete Declaration Under Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement Act (FL-105/GC-120).
Complete any additional forms needed for requested custody, parenting-time, support, or other orders.
Check whether the local court requires additional local forms.
File the forms and pay the filing fee or request a fee waiver.

procedures.title: Serve parentage papers
procedures.description: After filing, the other person must be formally notified of the parentage case.
steps: Choose a server who is at least 18 years old and is not a party to the case.
Have the server deliver the required filed papers using an authorized method.
Have the server complete the appropriate Proof of Service.
File the Proof of Service with the court.
Wait for the response period or proceed under the applicable next-step process.

procedures.title: Establish parentage using a Voluntary Declaration of Parentage
procedures.description: Eligible parents can establish parentage without first litigating a parentage case by properly completing and filing a VDOP.
steps: Confirm that both people are eligible to use a VDOP.
Sign the VDOP using an authorized signing method, such as at a hospital, qualifying government location, or before a notary.
File the signed VDOP with the California Department of Child Support Services Parentage Opportunity Program.
After filing, use the established parentage if later court orders for custody, parenting time, or support are needed.

procedures.title: Finalize a parentage case
procedures.description: A parentage case is completed by submitting final forms for court review and obtaining a signed judgment.
steps: Determine the correct finalization process based on whether there is a default, agreement, genetic testing, or trial.
Prepare the judgment and other required final forms.
Include applicable custody, parenting-time, child-support, or other final orders.
Submit the final forms to the court clerk.
Obtain the judge's review and signed judgment.

procedures.title: Ask the Local Child Support Agency to establish parentage
procedures.description: A parent can ask the Local Child Support Agency (LCSA) to open a case to establish parentage, and the agency can also seek child-support and health-insurance orders.
steps: Apply online or contact the Local Child Support Agency to request a case.
Provide the information needed for the agency to open the case.
The LCSA may file the court papers needed to establish parentage.
The LCSA can arrange genetic testing when needed.
The LCSA may also request child-support and health-insurance orders.
